title: The kernel of a surjection from a finite free module onto a module of finite presentation is of finite type (Stacks 01BP(1))
statement: Let $(X,\mathcal O_X)$ be a ringed space (for instance a scheme [def-pc-scheme] with its structure sheaf) and $\mathcal F$ an $\mathcal O_X$-module [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] of finite presentation, i.e. every point of $X$ has an open neighbourhood $U$ with an exact sequence $\mathcal O_U^{\oplus m}\to\mathcal O_U^{\oplus n}\to\mathcal F|_U\to0$ (Stacks, Modules, Definition 01BN). Let $r\ge0$ and let $\psi:\mathcal O_X^{\oplus r}\to\mathcal F$ be a surjective map of $\mathcal O_X$-modules. Then $\operatorname{Ker}(\psi)$ (the sub-$\mathcal O_X$-module $U\mapsto\ker\psi_U$) is of finite type: every point $x\in X$ has an open neighbourhood $V$ with a surjection $\mathcal O_V^{\oplus s}\to\operatorname{Ker}(\psi)|_V$ for some $s$ [pqf-def-coherent].

source.place: Modules, Lemma 01BP (label lemma-kernel-surjection-finite-free-onto-finite-presentation), part (1), line 1457, with its proof

proof.text: *Step 1 (maps out of finite free modules; kernels).* For an open $W\subseteq X$ and $n\ge0$, $\mathcal O_W^{\oplus n}$ is the finite direct sum, i.e. the product, of $n$ copies of $\mathcal O_W$, with $\mathcal O_W^{\oplus n}(V)=\mathcal O_X(V)^n$ for $V\subseteq W$; let $e_1,\dots,e_n\in\mathcal O_X(W)^n$ be the standard basis sections, and identify $\mathcal O_W^{\oplus m}\oplus\mathcal O_W^{\oplus r}=\mathcal O_W^{\oplus(m+r)}$. For an $\mathcal O_W$-module $\mathcal G$, a morphism $\varphi:\mathcal O_W^{\oplus n}\to\mathcal G$ is determined by the sections $\varphi_W(e_i)\in\mathcal G(W)$: every section over $V\subseteq W$ is $\sum_if_ie_i|_V$ with $f_i\in\mathcal O_X(V)$, and $\varphi_V(\sum_if_ie_i|_V)=\sum_if_i\,\varphi_W(e_i)|_V$ by $\mathcal O_X(V)$-linearity and compatibility with restriction; conversely, for any $s_1,\dots,s_n\in\mathcal G(W)$ this formula defines a morphism of $\mathcal O_W$-modules $\varphi_s$ with $\varphi_s(e_i)=s_i$ (it is $\mathcal O_X(V)$-linear on each $V$ and commutes with restrictions because restriction is semilinear) [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. In particular two morphisms out of $\mathcal O_W^{\oplus n}$ that agree on $e_1,\dots,e_n$ are equal. The kernel of a morphism $\psi$ of $\mathcal O_X$-modules is the sub-$\mathcal O_X$-module $V\mapsto\ker\psi_V$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]; hence for an open $U$, $\operatorname{Ker}(\psi)|_U=\operatorname{Ker}(\psi|_U)$, and a morphism $\gamma$ into the source of $\psi$ with $\psi\circ\gamma=0$ factors (uniquely) through $\operatorname{Ker}\psi$, the factorization having the same sections as $\gamma$.

source.place: Modules, Section 01AF (label section-kernels, lines 102-116: kernels are sectionwise and are kernels in Mod(O_X)); the correspondence between maps out of O^n and n-tuples of sections is used without comment in the proof of Lemma 01BP ('This gives a morphism of sheaves alpha')

proof.text: *Step 2 (a presentation near $x$, and the lifts $\alpha$, $\beta$).* Let $x\in X$. Since $\mathcal F$ is of finite presentation, choose an open $U\ni x$ and an exact sequence $\mathcal O_U^{\oplus m}\xrightarrow{\chi}\mathcal O_U^{\oplus n}\xrightarrow{\varphi}\mathcal F|_U\to0$. By [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-space-module-exactness-local-lifting](1) (on the ringed space $(U,\mathcal O_U)$) $\varphi$ is surjective as a map of sheaves. For $k=1,\dots,r$ the section $\psi_X(e_k)|_U\in\mathcal F(U)$ therefore lifts on the member containing $x$ of some open covering of $U$: there are an open $W_k$ with $x\in W_k\subseteq U$ and $\tilde e_k\in\mathcal O_X(W_k)^n$ with $\varphi(\tilde e_k)=\psi(e_k)|_{W_k}$. Likewise $\psi$ is surjective as a map of sheaves [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-space-module-exactness-local-lifting](1) (on $X$), so for $j=1,\dots,n$ there are an open $W'_j$ with $x\in W'_j\subseteq U$ and $b_j\in\mathcal O_X(W'_j)^r$ with $\psi(b_j)=\varphi(e_j)|_{W'_j}$. Replace $U$ by the open $U\cap\bigcap_kW_k\cap\bigcap_jW'_j\ni x$ (a finite intersection) and restrict $\chi,\varphi,\tilde e_k,b_j$ to it. The restricted sequence is still exact with $\varphi$ surjective: by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-space-module-exactness-local-lifting](1),(2) both properties are conditions on all opens $W$ of $U$ and their coverings, and those of the smaller $U$ are among them. By Step 1 let $\alpha:\mathcal O_U^{\oplus r}\to\mathcal O_U^{\oplus n}$ be the morphism with $\alpha(e_k)=\tilde e_k$ and $\beta:\mathcal O_U^{\oplus n}\to\mathcal O_U^{\oplus r}$ the one with $\beta(e_j)=b_j$. Then $\varphi\circ\alpha$ and $\psi|_U$ agree on every $e_k$, and $\psi|_U\circ\beta$ and $\varphi$ agree on every $e_j$, so by the uniqueness in Step 1: $\varphi\circ\alpha=\psi|_U$ and $\psi|_U\circ\beta=\varphi$.

source.place: Modules, Lemma 01BP, proof of (1), first paragraph (presentation over U; 'after shrinking U ... lift psi(e_k) ... This gives a morphism alpha with phi o alpha = psi. Similarly ... beta with psi o beta = phi'); Definition 01BN (label definition-finite-presentation, line 1378)

proof.text: *Step 3 (the map $\gamma$ lands in $\operatorname{Ker}\psi$).* Let $\gamma=(\beta\circ\chi,\ 1-\beta\circ\alpha):\mathcal O_U^{\oplus m}\oplus\mathcal O_U^{\oplus r}\to\mathcal O_U^{\oplus r}$, $(t,s)\mapsto\beta\chi(t)+s-\beta\alpha(s)$. Then, writing $\psi$ for $\psi|_U$: $\psi\circ\beta\circ\chi=\varphi\circ\chi=0$ (the presentation is a complex) and $\psi\circ(1-\beta\circ\alpha)=\psi-\varphi\circ\alpha=\psi-\psi=0$ (Step 2). So $\psi\circ\gamma=0$ and $\gamma$ factors through $\operatorname{Ker}(\psi|_U)=\operatorname{Ker}(\psi)|_U$ (Step 1).

source.place: Modules, Lemma 01BP, proof of (1), the displayed map (beta o chi, 1 - beta o alpha); that it lands in Ker(psi) is left implicit there

proof.text: *Step 4 (surjectivity onto $\operatorname{Ker}\psi$; conclusion).* Let $W\subseteq U$ be open and $s\in\mathcal O_X(W)^r$ with $\psi(s)=0$. Then $\varphi(\alpha(s))=\psi(s)=0$ (Step 2), so by exactness of the presentation at $\mathcal O_U^{\oplus n}$ [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-space-module-exactness-local-lifting](2) there are an open covering $W=\bigcup_iW_i$ and $t_i\in\mathcal O_X(W_i)^m$ with $\chi(t_i)=\alpha(s)|_{W_i}$. On $W_i$: $\gamma(t_i,s|_{W_i})=\beta\chi(t_i)+s|_{W_i}-\beta\alpha(s|_{W_i})=\beta\alpha(s)|_{W_i}+s|_{W_i}-\beta\alpha(s)|_{W_i}=s|_{W_i}$. Hence the factorization $\gamma:\mathcal O_U^{\oplus(m+r)}\to\operatorname{Ker}(\psi)|_U$ of Step 3 (same sections, $\operatorname{Ker}(\psi)|_U(W)=\ker\psi_W$) is surjective as a map of sheaves, i.e. a surjection of $\mathcal O_U$-modules [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-space-module-exactness-local-lifting](1). As $x$ was arbitrary, every point of $X$ has an open neighbourhood $U$ with a surjection $\mathcal O_U^{\oplus s}\to\operatorname{Ker}(\psi)|_U$, $s=m+r$: $\operatorname{Ker}(\psi)$ is of finite type [pqf-def-coherent] (the definition read on the ringed space $X$, as in the statement).
